adjudication_label: batch_9:work hardening dynamics and stress accumulation
canonical_question: Why does the work hardening in the <110> direction occur if the mechanism is dominated by mobile Shockley partials which reduce stress?

question_variants.question: Why does the work hardening in the <110> direction occur if the mechanism is dominated by mobile Shockley partials which reduce stress?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text explains that while Shockley partials are mobile, the immobile stair-rod dislocations result in an increase in stress, which contributes to work hardening, though it does not explicitly address the <110> direction anisotropy mechanism in detail.

answers.answer: Work hardening occurs because immobile stair-rod dislocations accumulate and result in an increase in stress, counteracting the stress reduction from mobile Shockley partials.
answers.measurement_outcome: Increase in stress due to immobile dislocations
answers.mechanism: Stair-rod dislocations, on the other hand, are immobile dislocations, and their presence results in an increase in stress.
evidence_spans: The primary dislocations observed were Shockley partial dislocations and stair-rod immobile dislocations.
No BCC atoms were observed in any of the three orientations, indicating that no FCC-to-BCC phase transformation occurred during tensile deformation.
The yield strength of the alloy was relatively insensitive to strain rate within the simulated range.
